items.title: State notification channel payload slimmed to a pointer
items.description: The platform-managed 'state' notification channel (NotificationTask state channel and the new state-level notification directive) no longer embeds the full State function output (GetInstanceStateOutput) in the message data. The data payload is now the slim pointer { domain, flow, id, version } inside the CloudEvents envelope; consumers must re-fetch the full state via the State function. Binding metadata and IStateNotificationMapping enrichment are unchanged.
items.action: Update state-channel consumers to treat the message as a change pointer and call the State function for full state instead of reading data.data.* fields.

items.title: Schema x-roles DENY now applies across the whole grant set
items.description: Field-level visibility used to evaluate each caller role against a path's grants in isolation, and a path was visible if any single role passed. A DENY naming a predefined role was therefore defeated whenever the caller also held some unrelated role: that role matched nothing, the deny-only set fell through to the blacklist rule, and the field stayed visible. Evaluation now runs the canonical rule over the whole grant set, so a matching DENY hides the field regardless of the caller's other roles. Fields previously exposed by this gap become hidden.
items.action: Review every schema declaring a DENY in x-roles. If a field was relied upon as visible while a DENY grant matched the caller, the declaration was not expressing that — replace the DENY with an explicit ALLOW list for the roles that should see the field.

items.title: Schema x-roles: a role-less caller now sees deny-only fields
items.description: A caller with no roles was rejected before the grant rule was applied, so a path guarded only by DENY grants was hidden from them. The canonical blacklist rule now applies: a grant set with no ALLOW grant allows anyone it does not explicitly deny, including a role-less caller. Note that a path guarded by an ALLOW grant is still hidden from a role-less caller, so allowlist declarations are unaffected.
items.action: If a field must never reach an unauthenticated or role-less caller, declare it with an explicit ALLOW list instead of relying on DENY grants alone.

items.title: Human-task list authorization now matches the transition-execution rule
items.description: The list split a transition's grants into static and predefined subsets, evaluated each separately and required BOTH to match. A transition declaring [allow: teller, allow: $InstanceStarter] was therefore only listed for a caller who was both a teller and the instance starter, even though either one alone was enough to execute it — the task was hidden from users who could act on it. The list now applies the same any-matching-ALLOW rule as execution and additionally honors dynamic $.context.* grants, which it previously ignored entirely. Expect more tasks to appear for the same caller.
items.action: Re-check human-task expectations for transitions that mix static and predefined grants. To require both conditions, model the second as a DENY for the complement rather than relying on the old AND behavior.

items.title: updateData no longer re-runs the state's OnEntry/OnExit or re-arms its timers
items.description: updateData previously ran the full pipeline: the current state's OnExit tasks ran, its OnEntry tasks ran a second time, and the state's scheduled transitions were cancelled and re-armed - restarting every timeout from zero. Those four steps (CancelScheduledJobs, OnExit, OnEntry, Schedule) are now excluded for updateData, whose target is fixed to the reserved $self key and which therefore leaves and enters no state. The transition's own onExecute tasks, the data write and the auto-transition evaluation are unchanged. This applies to updateData ONLY. Other transitions declaring target $self - shared transitions in particular - are unaffected and keep running the full state lifecycle, as do transitions naming the current state literally, including self-loops.
items.action: If a workflow relied on updateData re-running the current state's OnEntry to refresh something, move that logic into the transition's own onExecutionTasks. If it relied on updateData resetting the state's scheduled-transition timer, model the reset explicitly. Only the workflow-level updateData transition is affected, so no search of state transitions is needed. Note the converse for $self shared transitions, which are unchanged: because they still cancel and re-arm the state's scheduled transitions, a frequently invoked one on a state with a short timeout defers that timeout on every call.

items.title: Async chained transitions now continue in-process by default
items.description: An async transition's chained continuation (an automatic transition, an error-boundary rule's replacement transition, or an updateData handoff) now runs in-process inside the job already executing instead of being enqueued as its own scheduler job. This removes one scheduler round trip per hop. Trade-offs: there is no durable per-hop checkpoint (a crash mid-chain leaves the instance Busy under the accept's single InstanceJob row rather than resuming at the last committed hop), TransitionJobTimeoutSeconds now covers the WHOLE chain rather than one hop, and an inline chain leaves no per-hop job row so a mid-chain updateData is more likely to take over than to drop.
items.action: Review TransitionJobTimeoutSeconds against your longest auto-chain, not against a single transition. Set WorkflowExecution:AutoTransitionMode to "Scheduled" to keep the previous per-hop-job behavior. Replaces the removed TransitionPerJob flag. See docs/architecture/async-transition-execution-modes.md.

items.title: Transition span names now carry domain/flow/transition
items.description: Both transition-hop spans are renamed to {prefix}/{domain}/{flow}/{transition} — TransitionJob.Execute/... for a hop that ran as a scheduler job, and the new Transition.Hop/... for one that ran inline inside an already-executing job. The lane shape is unchanged (anchor-parented, predecessor linked, LaneSeq ordered, ActivityKind.Consumer so apm-server still classifies it as a transaction); only the names change. Every name segment is a definition-level identifier, so transaction cardinality stays bounded.
items.action: Dashboards, alerts and trace queries filtering on the exact name "TransitionJob.Execute" match nothing after this change — switch to a prefix match. Add the "Transition.Hop" prefix alongside it to keep counting chained hops once a domain runs with AutoTransitionMode: Inline. See docs/architecture/async-transition-execution-modes.md.

items.title: Transactional-outbox continuation path removed
items.description: The TransitionContinuationRequested contract, its Inbox relay handler and the internal POST .../transitions/{key}/enqueue endpoint are gone. The scheduler is the only delivery path. A failed enqueue is retried briefly (3 attempts) and then reported: the chained continuation faults the instance, and an async accept fails instead of returning 202 for work that may never be delivered.
items.action: Before upgrading, verify no TransitionContinuationRequested rows are pending in the outbox — nothing consumes them afterwards. Such rows only ever appeared as a direct-enqueue fallback, so the table is normally empty. See docs/architecture/async-transition-execution-modes.md.

items.title: Same-domain trigger tasks now nest under their Task.Execute span
items.description: A trigger-family task (StartTrigger, DirectTrigger, GetInstance, GetInstances, GetInstanceData, SubProcess) targeting the runtime's own domain dispatches in-process. Its target instance's spans previously anchored to the CALLING instance's trace lane and appeared as siblings of the caller's own hops. The local branch now opens a child lane on the Task.Execute span, so the triggered work is nested underneath the task that triggered it — the same shape a subflow handoff already had. Cross-domain routing is unchanged.
items.action: No action required. Traces gain a level of nesting under Task.Execute for locally triggered instances; queries that selected those spans by the root instance id tag (vnext.root.instance.id) are unaffected. See docs/runtime/trace-lanes.md.
